For a 50-person Indian company, the key point is that managed-travel pricing is usually quote-based, so the “total cost” is primarily your negotiated transaction fees plus the underlying airfare/hotel spend.

Option	Fee structure / cost	Cancellation & refunds	Warranty / service protection	Support
FCM Travel	Quote-based; request per-booking fees, implementation and account-management charges.	Supplier fare rules apply; FCM can manage changes/reissues.	No conventional product warranty; service levels should be contractual.	24/7 human support, India-specific platform, duty-of-care and disruption management. 
FCM Travel
+1

BCD Travel	Quote-based; negotiate online/offline transaction fees and programme-management costs.	Primarily governed by airline/hotel fare rules; require written reissue/refund SLA.	Contract/SLA rather than consumer-style warranty.	Dedicated account/service model; verify India after-hours coverage in proposal.
Amex GBT / Egencia	Custom pricing; Egencia says fees average <4% of overall travel spend and online bookings have lower fees. 
Egencia
	Fare/supplier rules apply; unused-ticket handling is an important cost lever.	No conventional warranty; contractual service terms.	Amex provides 24/7 programme support; BTA centralises air spend and offers up to ₹30 lakh accident cover, subject to policy terms. 
americanexpress.com
+1

For procurement, demand these numbers: booking fee, offline/agent fee, cancellation/reissue fee, hotel cancellation handling, implementation fee, annual minimum/commitment, GST, unused-ticket credits, and 24/7 response SLA.

Biggest hidden cost: cancellation/reissue handling and unused tickets—not the headline management fee.
